propositions: Rebar reconciler hardcodes project-specific workflow mappings (status, type, transitions, parent relationships) in core code, making it unable to support projects with analogous Jira concepts without editing the shipped codebase.
Mapping values are duplicated across three source files (value_maps.py, config.py, inbound_fields.py), creating consistency risk and requiring changes in multiple places to support new projects.

A provider-neutral, config-driven mapping seam must read per-project overrides from rebar.toml with layered composition (built-in default → config default block → per-project overlay) to decouple project-specific rules from core code.

Unmapped ticket types must be handled via collapse (round-trip-safe with rebar-type: labels), skip (type-level exclusion), or drift (diverge with warning), with load-time validation preventing undecided states.
Non-allowed transitions must be replayed by deriving the hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log and re-attempting each intermediate hop, falling back to drift if replay fails.
Non-representable parent relationships must drift with a breadcrumb comment naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key to maintain echo-safety.
